title: OpenAI announces a Superalignment team and pledges 20% of its secured compute over four years to it
summary: The team is co-led by Ilya Sutskever and Jan Leike and aims to solve alignment of superintelligent systems with human intent.

title: Sarah Silverman files a class action against Meta and OpenAI, alleging training on copyrighted books without permission
summary: Wikipedia's AI timeline dates the filing to 9 July 2023; the claim is an allegation of copyright infringement.

title: Anthropic releases Claude 2 through a public website and an API
summary: Anthropic made its second-generation Claude model available to the public.

title: California regulator delays its decision on Cruise and Waymo robotaxi expansion to 10 August
summary: The California Public Utilities Commission postponed the expansion hearing a second time.

title: Elon Musk announces xAI, a new AI company
summary: Musk said xAI would pursue a 'maximally truth-seeking' AI.

title: China publishes Interim Measures for generative AI services, effective 15 August
summary: Seven bodies led by the Cyberspace Administration set rules for public-facing generative AI providers on training data, content, user protection and supervision.

title: US FTC reportedly sends OpenAI a civil investigative demand over data security and privacy practices
summary: The demand concerns how OpenAI handled data and privacy in developing ChatGPT.

title: SAG-AFTRA actors begin a strike, with studio use of AI to scan faces among the stated causes
summary: The strike started on 14 July 2023 in Los Angeles and New York and covered the AMPTP studios.

title: Meta releases Llama 2, a language model free for research and commercial use, with Microsoft as a partner
summary: Meta and Microsoft introduced the next generation of Llama.

title: UN Security Council holds its first formal meeting on AI under the UK presidency
summary: Speakers called for an ethical, responsible international governance framework and warned of misinformation, misuse and autonomous weapons.

title: Leading AI companies, including OpenAI, make voluntary White House-coordinated commitments on safety and security
summary: The commitments cover areas such as red-teaming, protection of model weights and public reporting.

title: Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI launch the Frontier Model Forum
summary: The four companies set up an industry body for the safe and responsible development of advanced AI models.
